key_insight: Any2Building uses shared spatial queries to bring point-cloud geometry and image-based visual cues into a common 3D framework. It aims to reconstruct structured buildings from either input type or both together.
problem_solved: Partial point clouds capture incomplete building surfaces, while overhead images reveal footprints and roof features without directly measuring full 3D geometry. The challenge is to use these complementary observations within one reconstruction framework.
method: Accept partial point clouds, overhead images, or both as building observations.
Use shared spatial queries to align geometric and visual information in 3D.
Reconstruct structured buildings using the available cues; implementation and evaluation details are not provided in the truncated abstract.
impact: A unified approach could make building reconstruction more flexible when sensor inputs are incomplete or vary across locations. This is relevant to 3D urban modeling and digital twins, though the supplied excerpt does not establish performance gains.
visual_elements: Three input routes—point cloud, overhead image, and both—converging on one reconstructed building.
A shared 3D query grid linking image features with point-cloud geometry.
A complementary-cues diagram highlighting measured surfaces, building footprints, roof geometry, and rooftop structures.
An input-to-output illustration showing incomplete observations beside a structured 3D building.
paper_title: Any2Building: Unifying Point Clouds and Images for Building Reconstruction via Shared Spatial Queries
paper_authors: Hongye Hou, Zhuoxiao Li, Liu Xiangyu, Tengxi Wang, Jing Ou
